offer.title: Tell Scout what you care about
offer.lead: Three quick questions, all optional. Your answers become rules you can see before they are saved.

flow.footer: You can change this anytime in Scout’s memory.

always.title: Whose mail should always reach you?
always.lead: Their mail stays in your inbox and never gets filed away. These are the people you reply to most.
always.label: People to always see
always.noSenders: No mail yet to suggest from. Add an address or a domain below.

never.title: What never needs you?
never.lead: Scout keeps it and still sorts it. It just stops asking you about it. Mail that looks suspicious always shows.
never.label: What never needs you

add.label: Someone else
add.invalid: Write a full address (name@example.com) or a domain (example.com).
add.freeMail: {{domain}} is a free mail provider: a rule for all of it would match people you don’t know. Add the person’s address instead.

act.title: When Scout is sure, should it act?
act.lead: This is about rules Scout proposes after you correct the same thing a few times. In an inbox you share, they always wait for a yes.
act.label: When Scout is sure
act.askFirstHint: Scout proposes. Nothing changes until you say yes.
act.actThenTellHint: In an inbox only you use, Scout starts the rule and tells you, with Undo.

reviewStep.title: Here’s what Scout will do
reviewStep.rules_one: {{count}} rule. It runs on every new email, before any AI, and always gives the same result.
reviewStep.rules_other: {{count}} rules. Each runs on every new email, before any AI, and always gives the same result.
reviewStep.none: No rules. Scout keeps sorting your mail as it does today.
reviewStep.shared: For everyone: shared with other people. Off unless you switch it on.
reviewStep.readOnly: {{address}}: you can only read it, so no rules there.
reviewStep.existing: Also apply to the mail you already have
reviewStep.existingHint: Otherwise only new mail. You can undo either.
reviewStep.askFirst: When Scout proposes a rule from your corrections, it waits for your yes.
reviewStep.actThenTell: When Scout proposes a rule from your corrections in an inbox only you use, it starts it and tells you, with Undo.
reviewStep.failed: Scout couldn’t save everything. What was saved is listed in Scout’s memory; try again for the rest.

done.title: Scout knows what you care about
done.lead_one: {{count}} rule is on. You’ll find it in Scout’s memory.
done.lead_other: {{count}} rules are on. You’ll find them in Scout’s memory.
done.leadNone: Nothing changed. You can answer again anytime in Scout’s memory.

rule.alwaysFrom: Mail from {{who}} always stays in your inbox and never gets filed away.
rule.neverLists: Newsletters and mailing lists never need you.

header.list_id: it comes from a mailing list

act.asks_action_true: it asks you to do something
act.surface_always: keep it in your inbox and never file it away

rule.noMatches: No mail yet. It applies as mail arrives.

memory.title: Scout’s memory
memory.lead: What Scout knows about how you want it to act. Rules run first, on every email, without AI.

teach.title: Teach Scout something
teach.label: What should Scout do?
teach.placeholder: For example: anything from my accountant always matters
teach.privacy: Only your sentence is sent, never your mail.
teach.readingLead: Sent to the language model: your sentence, your inbox addresses and your stream and label names. Nothing from your mail.
teach.understoodMany: Here are the rules I understood
teach.whoLead: I only read your sentence, so point me at them. These are the closest people in your mail.
teach.whoNoMatch: No one in your mail matches. These are the people you reply to most.
teach.readOnly: You can only read your inboxes, so Scout can’t save rules in them.
teach.existing: Also apply to the mail you already have
teach.runsWithoutAi: Saved rules run without AI. The same email always gets the same result.
teach.closest: The closest rule Scout can make:

unsupported.sends_mail: Scout can’t send, forward or reply to mail. Rules only sort, label, archive, and show or hide it.
unsupported.deletes_mail: Scout can’t delete mail. Rules only sort, label, archive, and show or hide it.
unsupported.not_about_mail: That isn’t about your mail, so Scout can’t make a rule of it.
unsupported.too_vague: That doesn’t say which mail. Name a sender, a domain, or words in the subject.

teach.unclear: Scout couldn’t turn that into a rule. Try naming a sender, a domain or words in the subject, and what to do with that mail.
teach.failed: Scout couldn’t read your sentence just now. Try again in a moment, or build the rule yourself.
teach.busy: That’s a lot of sentences this hour. Try again later, or build the rule yourself.

refused.instruction_empty: Write what you want Scout to do with your mail.
refused.instruction_too_long: Keep it to 300 characters: one or two sentences.
refused.instruction_has_link: Leave links out. Say which mail, and what to do with it.
refused.instruction_pasted_mail: This looks pasted from an email. Say in your own words which mail, and what to do with it.

builder.noModel: This server has no language model for reading sentences, so build the rule here.

conditions.list: It comes from a mailing list

questions.title: Your answers
questions.askFirst: When Scout proposes a rule from your corrections, it waits for your yes.
questions.actThenTell: When Scout proposes a rule from your corrections in an inbox only you use, it starts it and tells you, with Undo.
questions.never: You haven’t answered Scout’s questions yet.
